To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Colonna Hey Grove capsular arthrodesis is a reliable operation for late presentation of congenital dislocations of the hip, with a high rate of good functional results, but that these results may deteriorate with time.
Forty four patients who underwent 50 capsular hip arthroplastie for congenital dislocations of the hip had a mean follow up period of 20 years (range 15–25) after the operation.

1) the long term results of Colonna Hey Grove arthroplasty are satisfactory; 2) the results are better in patients who are operated at an early age; 3) the results are worse in patients with bilateral arthoplasties; and 4) functional deterioration is more common after 10 years than before.
